title: MemAudit: Auditing Long-Term Agent Memory via Hidden User-State Recovery
abstract: arXiv:2606.24595v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Long-term memory promises LLM agents that grow more capable across sessions, maintaining an accurate, evolving understanding of the user that interaction forms. In practice, however, this memory is evaluated mostly through downstream behavior, such as later answers, personalization quality, or task success, which tests that understanding only indirectly and leaves the memory artifact itself largely unaudited. We argue that long-term memory should instead be evaluated as an auditable post-interaction artifact: after ordinary assistance, what structured user state can be reconstructed from the memory the agent leaves behind? translated_title: MemAudit：通过隐藏用户状态恢复来审计智能体长期记忆
translated_abstract: 长期记忆有望使LLM智能体在多次会话中能力持续提升，维持对用户的准确且不断演化的理解，而这种理解是由交互形成的。然而在实践中，这种记忆大多通过下游行为来评估，例如后续回答、个性化质量或任务成功与否，这只能间接检验上述理解，而记忆产物本身在很大程度上未被审计。我们认为，长期记忆应当作为一种可审计的交互后产物来评估：在完成普通的辅助任务之后，从智能体留下的记忆中能够重构出什么样的结构化用户状态？我们在MEMPROBE中实例化了这一观点，这是一个基准测试：配备记忆的智能体在一系列泄漏受控的任务轨迹中协助模拟用户，每个模拟用户都携带一个隐藏的、基于分类体系锚定的用户状态库，随后在完整存储和top-（摘要在此处截断）等设置下，从智能体产生的记忆中对该状态库进行重构。
tldr: 该论文提出应将LLM智能体的长期记忆作为可审计的交互后产物来直接评估，并构建了MEMPROBE基准，通过从智能体记忆中重构隐藏的结构化用户状态库来审计记忆本身的内容。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes evaluating LLM agents' long-term memory as an auditable post-interaction artifact, introducing MEMPROBE, a benchmark that audits memory content directly by reconstructing hidden, taxonomy-anchored user states from the agent's memory.
